title.home: Preflight: fly the whole run before you pay for it
nav.label: Preflight
home.eyebrow: A flight simulator for ML jobs
home.lede: Preflight runs a few minutes of your real training job, learns how it behaves, and lets you move any setting and watch memory, time and cost answer at once. GPU time is spent only to check the plan you pick.
home.scroll: Scroll to see how it works
home.probe.title: Probe
home.probe.body: Minutes of real steps on a real GPU. Every number starts from a measurement.
home.simulate.title: Simulate
home.simulate.body: Move a knob and the map, memory and cost answer in under 400 ms, computed in your browser.
home.verify.title: Verify
home.verify.body: When the plan looks right, one short real run confirms it before the long one starts.
home.closing: Catch the crash at the first eval before it costs you a night.

detail.label: Details for {name}
detail.about.data: Loading and tokenising runs on the CPU, so a faster GPU makes it a bigger share of the step, not a smaller one.
detail.about.forward: The model's blocks are drawn once with how many times they repeat. Activations from here are held until backward.
detail.about.loss: Cross-entropy over the vocabulary. Logits for long examples are a hidden memory cost.
detail.about.backward: Gradients flow back through every block. With checkpointing on, forward work is redone here and memory drops.
detail.about.optimizer: The optimiser keeps extra numbers for every trainable weight. With LoRA that is the adapters only.
detail.about.eval: Evaluation runs every few hundred steps at its own batch size. If it keeps activations, it can need more memory than training.
detail.about.checkpoint: Each save writes the trainable state to disk. On a preemptible queue, the gap between saves is the work you can lose.

guide.label: Guide
guide.intro: I'll walk you through the few knobs that matter most for this job, aiming for {aim}, and move each one on the map so you can see what it does.
guide.pin.help: Put it back and pin it so the guide moves on
guide.needs_code: This needs a code change. Muse Code writes it in a sandbox and a short verify run checks it.
guide.fallback: The live guide isn't available right now, so the rule-based tour is running instead.
guide.cliff: {knob} at {value} crosses the memory limit: peak {peak} of {cap}.
guide.done: That's the tour. No other single move improves your aim.
guide.done.why: The tour stops when no knob it may move improves the aim without risking a failure, or when every useful knob is pinned or already toured.
guide.nothing_safe: Something on the map is likely to fail, and no knob the model can answer for fixes it yet. Measuring the fix is the honest next step.
guide.nothing_safe.why: The fix sits outside what this record's predictions cover, so the guide won't guess. A probe at the fixed setting measures it; it costs a little GPU time and waits for your go-ahead.
guide.pin_blocks_fix: {knob} is pinned, and moving it to {to} is what would make the run fit.
guide.pin_blocks_saving: {knob} is pinned. Releasing it to {to} would change {target} by {delta}.
guide.pin_blocks.why: The guide never moves a pinned knob. When the aim can't be met with your pins, it names the pin in the way and what releasing it would buy.
guide.ask.label: What are you doing, and what matters most?
guide.ask.placeholder: Fine-tune a 7B model on our support tickets, one A100, done by Friday, cheapest possible.
guide.approval.run_probe: The guide wants to measure this on a real GPU. Measuring costs a little money, so it waits for you.
guide.approval.propose_patch: The guide wants Muse Code to write this code change. That costs a little money, so it waits for you.
guide.approval.run_verify: The guide wants one real run of this plan to verify it. That costs a little money, so it waits for you.
guide.approval.unavailable: Live measuring opens with the probe queue
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.fix.line: Your eval pass is the risk. At eval batch {from} it needs more memory than this GPU has, so the run would stop at the first eval. Eval batch {to} peaks at {peak} of {cap}, and changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.fix.why: Eval runs every few hundred steps at its own batch size. Here it keeps activations as if it were training, so at a large eval batch it holds more than the whole training step.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.save.line: An eval batch of {to} changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.eval_batch_size.save.why: Larger eval batches finish evaluation sooner, as long as they still fit beside the training state.
guide.rule.batch_size.fix.line: A batch of {to} instead of {from} fits in memory, and changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.batch_size.fix.why: Activations grow with batch size times sequence length, so a smaller batch shrinks them.
guide.rule.batch_size.save.line: A batch of {to} keeps the GPU busier: {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.batch_size.save.why: Small batches leave the GPU waiting between kernels. A larger batch does more work per launch, until memory runs out.
guide.rule.seq_len.fix.line: Sequences of {to} tokens instead of {from} fit in memory. That changes what the model sees, so check it suits your data.
guide.rule.seq_len.fix.why: Activations and logits grow with sequence length. Shorter sequences fit, but long examples get cut.
guide.rule.gradient_checkpointing.fix.li: Checkpointing frees activation memory so the run fits. Steps get slower: {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gradient_checkpointing.fix.wh: Checkpointing keeps only each block's input and recomputes the rest during backward, trading compute for memory.
guide.rule.gradient_checkpointing.save.w: Checkpointing saves memory at the cost of recomputation. It pays off when the freed memory lets a cheaper GPU or a bigger batch work.
guide.rule.gpu.fix.line: On {to}, the run fits in memory, and {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gpu.fix.why: A GPU with more memory removes the limit without touching the code.
guide.rule.gpu.save.line: Is a different GPU worth it? On {to}, {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gpu.save.why: A pricier GPU can be cheaper overall when it finishes fast enough. Predictions for a GPU that wasn't probed are extrapolated from its specs, so verify before you commit.
guide.rule.generic.fix.line: Moving {knob} from {from} to {to} makes the run fit, and changes {target} by {delta}.
guide.rule.generic.fix.why: Of the moves that clear the predicted failure, this one costs your aim the least.
guide.rule.generic.save.why: This is the knob whose best single move improves your aim the most without risking a failure.

guide.probe_offer: {knob} at {to} would change {target} by {delta}, but it's tight: a {chance} chance of running out of memory. Measure it before you rely on it?
guide.probe_offer.why: The guide only applies settings that fit. Tight means the prediction's range touches this GPU's limit, so one short real run settles it before the long one. Measuring costs a little GPU time and waits for your go-ahead.
guide.rule.gpu_type.fix.line: On {to}, the run fits in memory, and {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gpu_type.fix.why: A GPU with more memory removes the limit without touching the code.
guide.rule.gpu_type.save.line: Is a different GPU worth it? On {to}, {target} changes by {delta}.
guide.rule.gpu_type.save.why: A pricier GPU can be cheaper overall when it finishes fast enough. Predictions for a GPU that wasn't probed are extrapolated from its specs, so verify before you commit.
error.oom: Ran out of GPU memory during training.
error.oom.hint: Lower the batch size or sequence length, turn on checkpointing, or pick a GPU with more memory.
error.oom.eval: Ran out of GPU memory in the eval pass.
error.oom.eval.hint: Lower the eval batch, or run eval without gradients (torch.no_grad).
error.oom.host: Ran out of CPU memory on the machine, not the GPU.
error.oom.host.hint: Use fewer data workers, stream the dataset instead of loading it whole, or load the model in lower precision.
error.missing_package: A package the script imports isn't installed.
error.missing_package.hint: Add it to requirements.txt or the notebook's first cell, then check in again.
error.download_blocked: A download the script needs was blocked.
error.download_blocked.hint: Probes reach Hugging Face and PyPI only. Bundle the file, or point the script at a dataset on the Hub.
error.gated_model: The model is gated on Hugging Face.
error.gated_model.hint: Accept the model's licence on its Hub page and add a read token as a secret, or choose an open model.
error.file_not_found: The script looked for a file that isn't there.
error.file_not_found.hint: Upload the file with the script, or use a path relative to the repo.
error.cuda_error.hint: Often a kernel without support for this GPU or a bad index. Check the last lines of the log.
error.nccl.hint: Check the launcher settings; single-GPU probes don't need distributed setup.
error.dtype_unsupported: This GPU doesn't support the chosen precision.
error.dtype_unsupported.hint: Use bf16 on Ampere or newer, fp16 on older GPUs, or pick another GPU.
error.shape_mismatch.hint: Usually a sequence length or batch setting that the model or collator doesn't expect.
error.dataloader_worker.hint: Try fewer data workers, or zero to see the real error.
error.syntax_error: The script has a syntax error.
error.syntax_error.hint: Fix it locally first; the line is in the log.
error.script_exit: The script stopped on its own before training.
error.script_exit.hint: It may exit early on a missing argument or a check; see the last log lines.
error.too_few_steps: The probe finished too few steps to measure.
error.too_few_steps.hint: Raise max_steps above 2, or remove an early stop for the probe.
error.timeout: The probe ran past its time limit.
error.timeout.hint: Model download or data loading may be slow; a smaller split or cached model helps.
error.killed: The probe was stopped from outside.
error.killed.hint: Usually the sandbox's memory or time limit. Check in again, or try a smaller setting.
error.recorder: Preflight couldn't read this run's numbers.
error.recorder.hint: This one is on us. The run may still be fine; check in again or tell us.
error.user_error: The script raised an error of its own.
error.user_error.hint: The traceback in the log points to the line.
error.nan_divergence: The loss became NaN: the run diverged.
error.nan_divergence.hint: Lower the learning rate, add warm-up or gradient clipping, or use bf16 instead of fp16.
error.generic: Something went wrong in this probe.

guide.sample_offer: The run could cost anywhere from {lo} to {hi}, and your budget of {budget} sits inside that range. Running {tasks} more of its tasks for real narrows it enough to say whether it fits.
guide.sample_offer.why: The cost comes from a sample of the run's tasks, and a few long tasks can move the total a lot. More tasks shrink the range; the guide won't trade settings to save money until it knows whether you are over the budget. Sampling costs a little API money and waits for your go-ahead.
guide.approval.sample_more: The guide wants to run 20 more of your agent's tasks to narrow the cost range around your budget. That costs a little API money, so it waits for you.
guide.live.intro: Muse Spark will move the knobs that matter for your aim one at a time, on the map, and you decide each move.
guide.withheld: The guide's last reply quoted a number no tool returned, so it isn't shown. It has been told to quote only what the tools say.
guide.run.submitted: Queued: job {job}, position {position}. The result appears in this cockpit when it is measured.
guide.run.unavailable: Measuring isn't open yet, so nothing ran and nothing was charged.
guide.run.queue_full: The measuring queue is full right now. Try again in a little while.
guide.run.refused: That can't run for this record.
guide.run.failed: That didn't go through. Nothing was charged.
dial.off_scale: Past the end of this dial's scale
dial.scale.log: Scale runs from {lo} to {hi}; each step along the arc multiplies, so small and large runs both read
membar.untrusted.gap.help: The peak is {gap} more than the predicted parts add up to. That share isn't attributed, so treat it as unknown.
membar.untrusted.overshoot.help: The predicted parts add up to {over} more than the predicted peak. They're shown at their own sizes, not squeezed to fit, so trust the peak line over the parts.
membar.off_scale: Peak runs past this bar's scale
fitmap.title: Where it fits
fitmap.help: Each square is a setting you can fly to; press one to go there. The lines show where the run stops fitting, placed by predicted memory between the squares.
fitmap.risk: {risk} chance of running out of memory
fitmap.none: Fewer than two knobs change memory in this record, so there is no map to draw.
datause.title: What happens to your code
datause.sent: Checking in sends Preflight the repo link, your goal, the GPU you picked and what you wrote about the job.
datause.probe: Preflight fetches the repo and runs a few minutes of your job on a rented GPU on Modal, in a sandbox that holds none of Preflight's keys.
datause.script_map: Muse Spark, through Meta's Model API, reads your code to find the training loop.
datause.guide: If you use the live guide, your description, the flight record and your messages go to Muse Spark through Meta's Model API.
datause.record: The measurements, settings and map become a flight record, kept so the cockpit and its share link work. Anyone with the link can open it; nothing is listed publicly.
datause.retention: Your code is deleted {hours} hours after the probe, and records after {days} days.
datause.retention.unset: Nothing is deleted automatically yet, so only check in code you are happy for Preflight to keep.
datause.secrets: Never put keys or passwords in the repo; the sandbox can't use them and they could end up in the probe's logs.
datause.needed: Tick “I've read this” to check in.
guide.ask.datause: Your message goes to Muse Spark through Meta's Model API.
